questions.stem: What tends to characterise patients having urology surgery?
questions.answer: Often elderly, with many comorbidities including renal impairment

questions.stem: Why does anaesthesia for urology surgery vary so widely?
questions.answer: Procedures range from outpatient cystoscopy to major cancer surgery

questions.stem: Which findings suggest renal failure in a urology patient before surgery?
questions.answer: Haematuria or proteinuria, raised urea and creatinine, reduced creatinine clearance

questions.stem: In a urology patient with renal failure, what must be decided before surgery?
questions.answer: Acute or chronic, and the cause: prerenal, renal or postrenal (obstructive)
